payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 3: a dead-wire detector must not silently exclude a common source layout; the stated surface (verbsChecked) must equal what was read
payload.notes: Applying the adapter's three regexes to cli.py at this revision: 401 literal (parent, verb) registrations exist in the text and 334 are found line by line (66 of 92 root verbs, the rest nested). The 67 missed ones (debt, human-required, consensus, state compact and others) can never be reported dead, and the kernel_cli_surface metadata (334 verbs) overstates the checked surface. Only 7 add_subparser call sites pass a non-literal verb (the loops), so the loop account does not explain the gap. Whether any of the 67 verbs is dead cannot be read from the adapter's output; the root parser's 26 misses predate this package and it extends the same per-line read to the nested parsers. Close condition: Run REGISTER_RE over the whole file text, as SUBPARSERS_DEST_RE already is, and take the line from the match offset; add a fixture with a registration split across lines; closed when the production run registers 401 (dest, verb) pairs from literals and the fixture's multi-line dead verb is reported. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
